metadata.summary: The Shengqi (SQ) formula, comprising Danshen (DS) and Huangqi (HQ), is effective against acute myocardial infarction (AMI). While DS and HQ have distinct chemical profiles, their synergistic mechanisms remain unclear. We integrated RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to investigate the molecular and cellular basis of DS-HQ synergy in the AMI model. DS and HQ monotherapies restored 43.91% and 49.26% of AMI-associated genes, respectively, whereas SQ rescued 77.49% of these genes. Despite compositional differences, DS and HQ co-regulated angiogenesis-related targets. Single-cell analysis showed that SQ treatment activated microvascular endothelial subpopulations, enhanced reparative Spp1^hi macrophage polarization, and increased VEGFA secretion, thereby amplifying VEGFA–VEGFR signaling. Docking studies indicated that active compounds from DS and HQ bind distinct VEGFA domains, supporting structural synergy. DS and HQ synergistically promote angiogenesis and immune–endothelial crosstalk in AMI, offering new insights into combinational drug mechanisms in cardiovascular disease.

observations.text:
BackgroundRisk stratification for primary ventricular tachycardia/ventricular fibrillation (VT/VF) in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains limited. We aimed to identify gut microbiome biomarkers and microbial metabolic pathways associated with primary VT/VF in STEMI using machine learning (ML).

MethodsStool samples from 33 STEMI patients (7 with primary VT/VF and 26 without VT/VF) underwent full-length 16S rRNA sequencing during the acute ([≤]7 days) and recovery (30-60 days) phases. An ML pipeline integrating taxonomic features identified reproducible features associated with primary VT/VF. Core biomarkers were defined as taxa demonstrating both univariate significance (false discovery rate [FDR] <0.05) and multivariate classification importance. Functional pathways and enzymes were predicted using PICRUSt2.

ResultsFive acute-phase taxa were reproducibly associated with primary VT/VF: Clostridium aldenense, Enterocloster bolteae, bacterium NLAE-zl-G101, Alistipes shahii, and Roseburia sp. (all FDR <0.05). A reduced-feature support vector machine model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.846 (95% confidence interval, 0.676-0.984), with 85.7% sensitivity and 76.9% specificity. Differential abundance analysis showed enrichment of Bacteroides fragilis, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, and E. bolteae. Functional analysis demonstrated enrichment of fucose degradation and purine catabolism, with increased predicted abundances of L-fucose mutarotase and xanthine dehydrogenase.

ConclusionsPrimary VT/VF in STEMI was associated with a distinct gut microbiome-metabolic signature characterized by Lachnoclostridium-related taxa, persistent Bacteroides enrichment, and enhanced predicted fucose and purine metabolism. These exploratory findings warrant validation in larger independent cohorts and mechanistic studies.

Clinical PerspectiveWhat Is New? O_LIIn this exploratory cohort of 33 patients with STEMI, including 7 with primary VT/VF, an integrated microbiome and machine-learning framework identified five acute-phase microbial taxa associated with primary VT/VF and a coordinated predicted metabolic signature involving fucose and purine pathways.
C_LI

What Are the Clinical Implications? O_LIBecause stool sampling occurred after the arrhythmic event and the VT/VF subgroup was small, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than predictive; independent prospective validation is required before microbiome-derived markers can be considered for clinical risk stratification.

observations.text: Real-time fMRI neurofeedback can modify clinically relevant brain states, but transferring brain dynamics between peers has not been tested, particularly in addiction, where social learning is central to recovery. Here we introduce peer-guided movie neurofeedback (PG-MovieNF), which trains participants to align their brain activity with treatment-related dynamics derived from peers further along in recovery viewing the same movie. Using longitudinal fMRI data from individuals with opioid use disorder watching Trainspotting before and after 8 weeks of adjunctive treatment, we derived a multivariate treatment-predictive signal in dorsolateral and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex. An independent cohort then received real PG-MovieNF or yoked sham feedback during the same film. Real feedback increased alignment with the peer-derived target signal, reduced craving and improved affective ratings. Target alignment was coupled to shared orbitofrontal cortex dynamics during real feedback and predicted craving reduction. Together, these findings establish proof of concept for PG-MovieNF to enhance addiction recovery.
observations.title: Peer-guided movie neurofeedback to facilitate recovery in opioid use disorder

metadata.summary: Air pollution and extreme heat frequently co-occur, yet their combined effects on cardiac development following gestational exposure remain poorly understood. We investigated the effects and potential mechanisms of gestational co-exposure to low-concentration PM2.5 and heat. Pregnant mice were exposed to filtered air, PM2.5 (approximately 10 μg/m³), heat (39 ℃), or both for 2 h/day from embryonic day 6.5 (E6.5) to E18.5, and offspring hearts were evaluated on postnatal day 1 (P1). Gestational co-exposure increased ventricular wall thickness and impaired systolic function, accompanied by inflammatory cell infiltration, oxidative damage, and mitochondrial ultrastructural changes. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that co-exposure altered pathways related to energy metabolism, including inositol phosphate metabolism and pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis. Further analysis of the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) revealed concurrent reductions in myo-inositol levels and Ucp2 expression after co-exposure. Experimental validation further showed that co-exposure decreased ATP content, downregulated cardiac development-related genes, and increased the protein expression of DRP1 and FIS1. Collectively, these findings indicated that gestational co-exposure may impair cardiac development through mitochondrial dysfunction and suggested the potential involvement of myo-inositol/UCP2-related metabolic regulation, providing preliminary mechanistic insights into the developmental cardiotoxicity of combined environmental exposures.

observations.text: Most behavioral studies in animals investigate risk using outcome probabilities larger than 10%. However, real-world Decision-Making often requires evaluating events that are both extremely unlikely and highly consequential. To address this gap, we developed an experimental and computational framework to quantify how rats detect and adapt to rare (probability <1%) and extreme (deviation from mean >10 standard deviations) outcomes (REE). Using a four-armed bandit task, animals chose between options associated with probabilistic rewards (sugar pellets) or punishments (time-out delays). Depending on the animals choice, REE can occur or not, allowing us to probe how rats integrate information across both common and fat-tailed event distributions. Across subjects, behavior showed restricted diversification (typically two out of four options) and clear sensitivity to REE, expressed as a systematic avoidance of rare and extreme punishments (Black Swans) combined with partial exposure to rare and extreme gains (Jackpots). The dominant behavioral phenotype displayed a near-complete suppression of exposure to Black Swans, whereas exposure to Jackpots remained only moderate. This asymmetric sensitivity came at a cost: these animals accepted smaller frequent gains and larger frequent losses to avoid catastrophic outcomes. To account for these behaviors, we implemented an augmented reinforcement learning model in which REE are weighted separately from frequent events. Fitting this model to individual behavioral data captured subjects decision patterns far better than standard Q-learning, which systematically failed to reproduce the observed asymmetry. The best-fitting model suggests that the rat brain segregates information from the central outcome distribution and the distribution tails, assigning distinct value weights to REE during action selection. This work provides the first evidence that rodents spontaneously adapt their learning strategies to avoid extreme punishments while partially maintaining exposure to rare and extreme gains, suggesting that frequent outcomes are treated separately from rare and extreme ones through different weights in Decision-Making.
observations.title: Specific Sensitivity to Rare and Extreme Events: Quasi-Complete Black Swan Avoidance vs Partial Jackpot Seeking in Rat Decision-Making

metadata.summary: Haploinsufficiency of the RNA splicing regulator, RBFOX2, has been linked to congenital heart disease (CHD), yet its pathogenic mechanisms and contributions to heart failure (HF) risk remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that RBFOX2 is essential for progressing cardiomyocyte (CM) differentiation by shifting exon usage profiles to more mature states in genes encoding sarcomere, cytoskeletal, and focal adhesion components. Furthermore, this maturation program is initiated by RBFOX2 self-splicing at mutually exclusive exons encoding early and late isoforms with distinct functional roles. In heterozygous CMs, self-splicing is disrupted, which skews RBFOX2 isoform ratios and generates dominant-negative isoforms caused by faulty exon co-inclusion. Finally, we demonstrate that overexpression of correctly spliced ALPHA-ACTININ 2 rescues het, but not null, phenotypes by restoring contractility, which triggers a mechanosensing feedback loop involving RBFOX2 upregulation and transcriptome maturation. Collectively, our data suggest that decreased RBFOX2 dosage and self-splicing contribute to CHD pathogenesis and increase HF risk susceptibility.

metadata.summary: Human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) have the ability to self-differentiate forming anteroposterior-patterned three-dimensional structures, referred to as human 3D-gastruloids (h3D-gastruloids). Yet, the development of h3D-gastruloids in vitro relies on hESC-intrinsic mechanisms, which are largely unknown. Here, we demonstrate that the formation of gastruloids depends on the levels of the Hippo effector YAP1. By combining chemical and genetic approaches across multiple genetic backgrounds, we found that nuclear YAP1 activity impedes symmetry breaking of the gastruloids, while its inhibition enhances axial elongation, compared to controls. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) analysis reveals that YAP inhibition enhances anteroposterior elongation by accelerating the differentiation of hESCs toward the cardiac trajectory, facilitating the formation of an anterior pole in the h3D-gastruloids. Mechanistically, YAP controls differentiation timing by selectively regulating Polycomb/EZH2 binding on cardiac lineage genes.  In conclusion, our study underscores a pivotal role of YAP1 in 3D gastruloids and highlights the existence of an epigenetic hierarchy that shapes early developmental trajectories through gene expression modulation.

observations.title: YAP levels regulate anteroposterior elongation of hESC-derived gastruloids

observations.text:
IntroductionLow bone mineral density (BMD) is associated with altered bone remodeling and osteoimmune regulation. We aimed to prioritize transcript-level signals supported across human expression cohorts and evaluate their attribution within local cis-regulatory architecture.

Materials and MethodsNominal differential-expression signals from GSE56815 were restricted with a predefined 25-term MSigDB thematic library. Features measurable in GSE56815 and GSE2208 underwent linear SVM ranking, LASSO, and XGBoost selection, followed by cross-cohort transcriptomic assessment. OCEL1 was examined in a four-exposure locus-aware CisMRBEEX model with NR2F6, MRPL34, BABAM1, eQTLGen cis-eQTLs, heel eBMD GWAS statistics, and UKBB337K LD.

ResultsThe expression screen identified 2,568 genes at nominal P<0.05; thematic restriction retained 190 candidates and 107 common features entered machine learning. Linear SVM, LASSO, and XGBoost retained 24, 18, and 9 genes and converged on CPNE1, EZR, and OCEL1. Only OCEL1 showed concordant expression direction with P<0.05 in both cohorts. In the primary 268-variant four-exposure model, OCEL1 was positively associated with heel eBMD ({beta}=0.010293, SE=0.004107, 95% CI 0.002244-0.018342, P=0.01220, PIP=0.4001; conditional coefficient on the standardized analysis scale); BABAM1 retained an oppositely directed component. The no-palindromic reconstruction remained positive with wider uncertainty ({beta}=0.007652, P=0.06739).

ConclusionConvergent transcriptomic evidence prioritized OCEL1, whose conditional genetic-expression component was positively associated with heel eBMD after local shared cis regulation was modeled.

metadata.summary: Catecholamine-induced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) is associated typically with mutations in genes encoding Ryanodine Receptor type 2 (RYR2) and Calsequestrin 2 (CASQ2). RyR2 and Casq2 along with membrane proteins, junctin and triadin, constitute the Ca2+ release channel in the junctional sarcoplasmic reticulum in mammalian cardiomyocytes. Mouse models ablating the Casq2 gene phenocopy CPVT have been used to understand the molecular defects underlying the disease and to identify novel therapies. In this study we analyze roles for development and normal aging in the cardiac dysfunctions of Casq2-mutant mice. We show that aging intensifies the disease phenotype. Age-dependent changes in triadin but not in RyR2 or junctin correlate with a more severe CPVT phenotype. We also examine transcriptomes at 1 month and 2 years of age. We identify 583 genes whose expression is dependent on Casq2 genotype with enrichment for genes associated with calcium handling and transport, sarcomere structures, extracellular matrix, and stress signaling associated with cardiac failure. 37% of the differentially expressed genes are specifically dysregulated in older mice. These findings establish aging as a powerful modifier of CPVT and suggest that targeting structural protein dynamics and compensatory transcriptional pathways may offer new therapeutic strategies.

observations.title: Impact of aging on catecholaminergic ventricular arrhythmia and cardiac transcriptome of cardiac calsequestrin null mice

metadata.summary: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is one of the most common medical complications during pregnancy, characterized by hyperglycemia detected in either early or late pregnancy. It is associated with both short-term and long-term cardiovascular consequences in offspring, including cardiac hypertrophy and impaired cardiac function. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the role of the Wnt/β-catenin/Tcf7l2 pathway in GDM-induced cardiovascular effects on offspring. A mouse model of GDM was developed, revealing cardiac hypertrophy accompanied by activation of the Wnt/β-catenin/Tcf7l2 pathway in the heart. Cardiac-specific knockdown of β-catenin alleviated GDM-induced cardiac hypertrophy in offspring, while cardiac-specific overexpression of β-catenin exacerbated it. Treatment with saxagliptin mitigated GDM-induced cardiac hypertrophy in offspring by suppressing the Wnt/β-catenin/Tcf7l2 pathway. These findings suggest that the Wnt/β-catenin/Tcf7l2 pathway plays a pivotal role in GDM-induced cardiac hypertrophy in offspring, with saxagliptin offering potential therapeutic benefits through pathway inhibition.

observations.title: Inactivation of Wnt/β-catenin attenuates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced cardiac hypertrophy.

observations.text:
BackgroundMarijuana is among the most widely used controlled substances, with use rising as risk perception declines. Despite growing acceptance, concerns remain regarding its effects on cardiovascular and autonomic physiology, sleep, and risk of cannabis use disorder. Although laboratory and epidemiological studies have characterized these associations, objective evidence from real-world settings is limited.

MethodsWe studied cardiac autonomic function, sleep, and marijuana use patterns in 16,965 consumer-wearable device users, contributing a total of 5,226,739 person-days of data with or without self-reported use of marijuana. Linear mixed models related day-level use to nocturnal cardiac autonomic function (resting heart rate [RHR], heart rate variability [HRV]) and sleep (duration, fragmentation, architecture) at the within- and between-person levels. Binomial mixed models were used to estimate use probability across 72 weeks of marijuana tracking.

ResultsMembers reported marijuana use on a median of 25.1% of logged days (IQR, 7.1-62.6%). Within individuals, use was associated with lower RHR (-0.12bpm; 99.5% CI: [-0.14, -0.10]) and lower HRV (-0.47ms [-0.53, -0.42]). Sleep was longer (+7.60min [7.37, 7.83]) but more fragmented, with more disturbances (+0.47 [0.45, 0.48]), greater wake time (+1.79min [1.70, 1.89]), and altered wearable-estimated sleep architecture. Daily use probability declined over 72 weeks (-11.1% [-11.5, -10.8]).

ConclusionsMarijuana use was associated with altered nocturnal cardiac autonomic physiology and longer but more disrupted sleep. Marijuana use declined after commencing tracking, raising the possibility that longitudinal self-monitoring may influence use. These findings extend laboratory evidence on marijuana use to real-world settings and demonstrate the potential of consumer wearables for studying substance use and its physiological correlates at scale.

HighlightsO_LIMarijuana-use nights were associated with lower resting heart rate and heart rate variability.
C_LIO_LISleep was prolonged but more fragmented with marijuana use.
C_LIO_LIMarijuana use fell over 72 weeks of wearable tracking.

metadata.summary: Regular exercise reduces all-cause mortality, yet its molecular effects across organs, sexes, and circadian phases remain incompletely understood. We subjected mice to 8-week voluntary wheel running and collected 22 tissues and plasma during the inactive and active phases, profiling bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, proteomics, and single-nucleus RNA and methylation sequencing. Exercise induced canonical fiber-type switching and widespread, tissue-specific remodeling, with the largest transcriptomic changes in skeletal muscle. Most tissues changed more during the active phase; kidney and lung, during the inactive phase. Females showed broader transcriptional responses, with distinct downregulation. Pairing single-nucleus methylomes with transcriptomes resolved, at single-cell and single-base resolution, which cell types drive exercise-induced epigenetic remodeling, unresolved by bulk studies: coordinated gene-body demethylation and transcription tracked fiber-type switching in specific myonuclei, and cell-type-resolved methylation—including partially methylated domains characterized in muscle for the first time—revealed a strong, sex-biased epigenetic training response. Machine learning identified conserved cross-mammalian exercise signatures.

metadata.summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common persistent arrhythmia worldwide, and hypertension is one of the most important risk factors for AF, affecting its occurrence and maintenance. This study investigated the role of enolase 1 (ENO1) in hypertension induced atrial fibrillation. Our study found that ENO1 is continuously upregulated in the atria of hypertensive rats. Subsequently, an angiotensin II (Ang II) - induced atrial myocardial cell injury model was established to evaluate the role of ENO1 in Ang II induced myocardial cell injury. Transcriptomic analysis and enrichment analysis of ENO1 knockdown in primary atrial cardiomyocytes showed that ENO1 regulates the expression of mitochondrial NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4) through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, thereby regulating the production of reactive oxygen species and mitochondrial function. In vitro, the use of ENO1 knockout and ENO1 blockade (AP-III-a4) reduced Ang II induced ROS accumulation and atrial myocardial cell damage, while inhibiting the PI3K/AKT/NOX4 axis. In the Ang II induced mouse model, treatment with ENO1 inhibitors reduced pathological atrial hypertrophy and fibrosis compared to Ang II alone. In vivo, ENO1 inhibitors also reduced PI3K/AKT phosphorylation, NOX4 expression, and atrial ROS accumulation, subsequently improving atrial electrical remodeling, atrial fibrillation induction, and atrial fibrillation duration. These findings suggest that ENO1 is associated with hypertension related atrial remodeling and susceptibility to atrial fibrillation, and may be a potential therapeutic target.

metadata.summary: Aims: Recurrent in-stent restenosis (RISR) represents a series of repeated cardiac ischemic events post-successful revascularization, associated with exceedingly huge disease burden without effective pharmacologic therapies. Neointimal hyperplasia (NIH) is recognized as the primary biological driver that fundamentally triggers restenosis, yet the underlying immune mechanisms governing smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotypic transitions remain unclear. Methods：Coronary blood samples from ten RISR patients and ten control individuals were subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). Key pathogenic targets and pathways were identified through comprehensive bioinformatics analyses and further validated via in vitro experiments with monocytes isolated from the validation cohort using flow cytometry. Results: Here, scRNA-seq analysis revealed the prominent role of monocytes in driving RISR progression, with activator protein-1 (AP-1) genes emerging as core differentially expressed genes (DEGs). In vitro experiments within monocytes further demonstrated that the CCL5-CCR1/p38 MAPK pathway acts as an upstream regulatory axis of AP-1, promoting the release of inflammatory cytokines and ultimately inducing a phenotypic switch in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Additionally, a novel monocyte subtype was identified in coronary blood and the distinct alterations of subtype composition were specifically observed throughout the progress of RISR. Conclusion: This study provides the first comprehensive immunological landscape of RISR, thus offering theoretical support for clinical interventions. Upregulation of the CCR1/p38 MAPK/AP-1/cytokine axis in monocytes was identified as a critical mechanism facilitating the occurrence and progression of RISR.

metadata.summary: During organogenesis, the establishment of tissue architecture requires precise RNA processing. Many developmentally essential exons bear weak 5′ splice sites (5′SS) yet are spliced with high precision, implying unknown yet active splicing fidelity mechanisms. Combining transcriptome and alternative splicing profiling and with temporal eCLIP mapping of RNA interactions across development, we identify the RNA-binding protein QKI as an essential direct regulator of splicing fidelity in key cardiac transcripts. Although QKI is dispensable for cardiac lineage specification, its loss disrupts sarcomere assembly despite intact expression of sarcomere mRNAs through exon skipping and intron retention in key sarcomeric mRNAs.  QKI-dependent exons in essential cardiac genes have weak 5′SS  and frequently show poor complementarity with U6 snRNA; we show that QKI directly interacts with U6 snRNA using an overlapping interface to its traditional intronic binding activity, securing U4/U6·U5 tri-snRNP recruitment to ensure exon inclusion. Thus, QKI exemplifies how context-aware RBPs enforce splicing fidelity at structurally vulnerable splice sites by coupling local intronic cues to spliceosome engagement, thereby securing accurate exon inclusion during organogenesis.

observations.title: QKI ensures splicing fidelity during cardiogenesis by engaging the U6 tri-snRNP to activate splicing at weak 5’splice sites [RNA-Seq 2]

metadata.summary: Hybrid grouper (Epinephelus fuscoguttatus♀ × Epinephelus lanceolatus♂) are an essential species in marine aquaculture. However, they are susceptible to high temperatures, which can reduce disease resistance, slow growth rates, and decrease production efficiency, resulting in significant economic losses. This study aims to investigate the differences in heat tolerance between hybrid grouper and their parental species, tiger grouper (Epinephelus fuscoguttatus) and giant grouper (E. lanceolatus), and to identify heat stress-related signaling pathways and key genes. Through controlled temperature experiments, we measured the physiological and biochemical parameters of serum (ACP, AKP, TG, COR) and liver (HSP70, HSP90, SOD, CAT) in pearl gentian grouper and their parents, followed by liver transcriptome analysis of the three grouper species. The results showed that the lethal temperature of tiger grouper is 41℃, and the lethal temperature of hybrid tiger grouper and saddle grouper is 40℃. Significant changes in antioxidant and heat stress-related indicators were observed in the early stages of stress. Comparative analysis of DEGs related to heat tolerance between pearl gentian grouper and their parents revealed common DEGs including the hsp family, danaj family, slc family, pnpla2, magot, actalb, and prodh. Among these, the gene expression trends in hybrids were similar to those of their maternal parent and varied between the same or opposite trends compared to those of their paternal parent. These findings suggest that the hybrids inherit heat regulation genes from both parents, with a higher proportion from the maternal parent, which likely explains their intermediate heat tolerance. This research provides insights into the potential relationship between heat tolerance in pearl gentian grouper and their parents and identifies key genetic information affecting heat tolerance.

metadata.summary: BACKGROUND: Haploinsufficiency of the RNA splicing regulator, RBFOX2, has been linked to congenital heart disease (CHD), including hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain unresolved.  METHODS: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) heterozygous or null for RBFOX2 were created and their cardiomyocyte derivatives (iPSC-CMs) characterized in monolayer culture and engineered heart tissues (EHTs). In addition to cellular phenotyping, molecular profiling by RNA-sequencing and eCLIP-sequencing was performed to detect changes in gene expression, exon usage, and RBFOX2 binding. These datasets were integrated with each other to identify RBFOX2-bound RNAs with altered expression and/or splicing and with publicly available datasets from progressive CM differentiation timepoints. Rescue experiments were performed in iPSC-CMs, EHTs, and zebrafish. RESULTS: We demonstrate that RBFOX2 is essential for cardiomyocyte (CM) differentiation by driving transcriptome maturation through gene expression- and alternative splicing-based isoform switching in transcripts primarily encoding sarcomere, cytoskeletal, and focal adhesion components, including the critical Z-disc factor alpha-actinin-2 (ACTN2). We further demonstrate that threshold levels of RBFOX2 facilitate autoregulatory splicing at mutually exclusive exons encoding early and late RBFOX2 isoforms with distinct molecular functions. In heterozygous CMs, this threshold is never reached, resulting in isoform imbalance and production of an aberrant transcript, which further reduces functional RBFOX2 mRNA levels below 50% of WT. Finally, we demonstrate that ACTN2 overexpression rescues heterozygous, but not null, phenotypes, suggesting that ACTN2 activates an RBFOX2-dependent mechanosensitive feedback loop that promotes transcriptome maturation. CONCLUSIONS: Our data demonstrate that reduced RBFOX2 dosage and autoregulation stalls CM differentiation by inhibiting transcriptome maturation, contributing to CHD pathogenesis and potentially increasing heart failure susceptibility.

observations.title: RBFOX2 autoregulation promotes cardiomyocyte transcriptome maturation and differentiation

metadata.summary: Haploinsufficiency of the RNA splicing regulator, RBFOX2, has been linked to congenital heart disease (CHD), yet its pathogenic mechanisms and contributions to heart failure (HF) risk remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that RBFOX2 is essential for progressing cardiomyocyte (CM) differentiation by shifting exon usage profiles to more mature states in genes encoding sarcomere, cytoskeletal, and focal adhesion components. Furthermore, this maturation program is initiated by RBFOX2 self-splicing at mutually exclusive exons encoding early and late isoforms with distinct functional roles. In heterozygous CMs, self-splicing is disrupted, which skews RBFOX2 isoform ratios and generates dominant-negative isoforms caused by faulty exon co-inclusion. Finally, we demonstrate that overexpression of correctly spliced ALPHA-ACTININ 2 rescues het, but not null, phenotypes by restoring contractility, which triggers a mechanosensing feedback loop involving RBFOX2 upregulation and transcriptome maturation. Collectively, our data suggest that decreased RBFOX2 dosage and self-splicing contribute to CHD pathogenesis and increase HF risk susceptibility.

observations.text: A series of internal states, proceeding from curiosity (drive state) to insight (uncertainty reduction) to pleasure (reward and reinforcement), might represent a fundamental pathway for motivated learning. Here we present a paradigm that combines measurement of curiosity, insight (aha), understanding and liking to outline the contours of this epistemic arc and trace their neuronal correlates. In two preregistered experiments we employ the "title effect" - the fact that additional semantic information can change how one understands and enjoys a piece of art. Participants viewed paintings and rated their curiosity for seeing the title. This was followed either by the original title or a dummy title lacking additional information, and a second presentation of the image, after which participants rated their strength of aha, aesthetic liking, and feeling of understanding the artwork. In a behavioral study (N=55 participants) we establish empirically that visual art with their titles can prompt strong feelings of aha. The association between ratings is complex and shaped by the type and amount of information in the stimuli; e.g. aha is linearly linked to liking and nonlinearly to understanding. In an EEG, ECG and eye tracking study with the same paradigm (N=49 participants) we use time-resolved decoding to trace the temporal sequence of processing. Understanding can be decoded from various (neuro)physiological correlates, over extended timespans. Robust decoding of curiosity both before and after the titles substantiates its relevance within the epistemic arc. Aha could be decoded from pupil size, but not from the EEG. Lastly, a fast initial EEG response was linked to aesthetic liking. Though much remains to explore, our study provides a new window into core behavioral and physiological properties of motivated information foraging.
observations.title: Tracing the epistemic arc: Distinct physiological signatures for curiosity, insight, understanding and liking when viewing visual art

metadata.summary: Alcohol misuse damages numerous organs, including the liver, heart, brain, and pancreas. The kidney remains a severely understudied target of alcohol-induced injury despite renal injury being commonly observed in endstage alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) patients. A 6-week murine ethanol (1-6% v/v) model for earlystage ALD combined with carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) treatment was utilized to reveal mechanisms of renal injury. This paradigm yields elevated kidney damage markers when compared to ethanol consumption alone, including elevated urinary KIM-1 in 3 weeks. Hypothesis-generating tissue spatial analysis was used to explore ethanol-related transcriptomic alterations across kidney morphology. Using a publicly available scRNA-seq dataset, the predominant cell-type specific differences were identified and allowed for the generation of spatially resolved gene clusters. Ethanol + CCl4 increased kidney injury marker gene expression in proximal tubule cells, signifying extensive damage. Overall, a decrease in expression of ethanol metabolizing genes was localized to the renal cortex. Genes associated with the unfolded protein response (UPR) were induced across the kidney and were morphologically associated throughout the nephron. Key mRNAs (Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Ndrg1) and ribosomal transcripts were altered due to ethanol metabolism across proximal tubules. Furthermore, epigenetic alterations in regulatory marks of lysine acetylation or trimethylation are associated with the combination treatment. Collectively, the application of tissue spatial transcriptomics to a well-defined model of alcohol toxicity reveals dynamic morphologic changes in gene expression across renal cell types due to ethanol. Our results indicate ER stress and the UPR are significantly impacted by ethanol metabolism throughout proximal tubules, associating with ethanol-induced renal dysfunction.

observations.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals ER stress due to alcohol-induced kidney injury

metadata.summary: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with immune-mediated processes increasingly recognized as important contributors to CVD onset and progression. Seropositivity rates indicate 60–90% of the population carries latent viral infections, e.g., with cytomegalovirus, that profoundly shape the individual immune phenotype. Epidemiological studies have consistently associated cytomegalovirus (CMV) seropositivity with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, yet the functional consequences of latent CVM cytomegalovirus latency in the context of myocardial infarction (MI) have not been studied, nor has its underlying influence on cardiac tissue. In this study we employed a murine model of cytomegalovirus (MCMV) infection to investigate the impact of the virus in the cardiac immune environment. We characterized the immune cell populations involved in cardiac immune responses by flow cytometry and performed bulk RNA seq of infected and naive mice to dissect the transcriptional differences that occur after viral exposure. To better understand how viral infections affect the myocardium of infected and naive animals post MI, we conducted a series of experiments involving flow cytometry, single-cell RNA / TCR sequencing, echocardiography, and cMRI 5 days after mice underwent experimental MI. Additionally, we used cMRI to stratify CMV-seropositive patients as “good” or “poor healers” and tested their CMV IgG titers. Using TCR-sequencing, we also identified CMV-responding TCRs and compared blood-derived and heart-derived T cells from post-mortem tissues. Our findings show that exposure to murine CMV induces both long-term changes in the cardiac transcriptional profile and alterations in cardiac immune cell populations. We detected the establishment of virus-specific resident memory T cells that persist in cardiac tissue. Following myocardial infarction (MI), mice previously exposed to MCMV had more abundant cardiac-resident T cells, heightened inflammatory profile, and adverse ventricular remodeling, as revealed by MRI, compared to naive controls. These murine observations were supported by data from CMV-seropositive MI patients, who harbored CMV-responsive T cells and exhibited impaired cardiac healing. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that latent CMV infection leads to long-term immunological changes in cardiac tissue that exert significant effects on post-MI healing outcome.

observations.title: Cytomegalovirus latency exacerbates cardiac inflammation and tissue remodeling after myocardial infarction

metadata.summary: Wugang copper goose is an indigenous Chinese meat-type goose breed, but the regulation of leg muscle development during the embryonic-to-early post-hatch transition remains unclear. We combined serial histological analysis of breast and leg muscles from E15 to P1 with transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiling of leg muscle at E15, E23, and P1. Histological observations showed progressive organization of leg muscle fibers and bundles, with E23 representing a major transition point in structural maturation. The E15-to-E23 transition involved 1,472 differentially expressed genes, 475 differentially expressed proteins, and 334 differentially abundant metabolites, reflecting reduced replication-related signatures and increased molecular features related to sarcomere organization, creatine metabolism, and lipid handling. The E23-to-P1 transition involved 1,790 differentially expressed genes, 645 differentially expressed proteins, and 580 differentially abundant metabolites, mainly reflecting post-hatch structural maturation, oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid metabolism, and glycerophospholipid remodeling. Cross-omics integration identified coordinated modules involving DNA replication, cytoskeletal organization, energy metabolism, and lipid remodeling, and qPCR validation of 8 genes supported the RNA-seq trends. These results define a developmental trajectory from an early myogenic/proliferative state at E15, through a structural and metabolic transition at E23, to post-hatch maturation at P1 characterized by enhanced lipid-energy remodeling. This study provides candidate molecular modules for understanding goose leg muscle growth and meat-type trait development.

observations.title: Integrated histological, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses reveal stage-specific regulation of leg muscle development in Wugang copper goose
